changes.after: Its matrix-product complexity argument assumes efficient state preparation. The toxicity study supplies no RBFE planning result. The supplied research supplement reports that the inspected implementation uses analytic simulator expectations, not measured finite-shot hardware outputs. It also reports that the ordinary classical convolutional baseline differs from the quantum route in input normalisation as well as weight parameterisation: the quantum and transferred classical paths normalise input patches, whereas the ordinary scratch classical baseline does not. Comparable reported predictive performance therefore does not isolate a quantum training effect under matched inputs and parameterisation. These are attributed implementation findings, corroborated along the retained reproduction and source-history path; dated source lines and byte identity narrow provenance but do not establish which exact implementation produced the publication runs. They do not invalidate the stated instantaneous transfer map.\footnote{Supplied research supplement: branch-1 entry 24, branch-2 entry 5, and branch-3 entries 80 and 87. These are recorded source inspections, not new execution or independent inspection for this account.}

Neither absence nor novelty follows.

Branch-2 also records directly relevant planning and loading-aware neighbours. Its corrected HiMap attribution concerns an explicit question about how random or noisy weights can become while optimal designs remain efficient, recovered from indexed text of the archived author manuscript, rather than an independently checked publisher version of record. Direct repository/PMC access met bot checks and attempted PDF downloads returned no content; that version and access limitation must accompany the attribution. The branch also reports that Landman's neural-network work counts classical loader preprocessing, unary-loader gates and depth, and repeated measurements for dense-network inner products. That unary construction uses a different encoding from P's logarithmic-qubit preparation. These are descriptions of the retained branch's source inspections; the HiMap manuscript and Landman primary text are not independently supplied here. They identify prior coverage of broad noisy-weight robustness and loading-aware inner-product costs, without establishing this specific RBFE compiled-cost curve or its novelty.\footnote{Supplied research supplement: branch-2 entries 47 and 51, with the HiMap version correction in entry 70. No new search or primary-source verification is claimed.}
